papers.title: Video Generation Models are General-Purpose Vision Learners

summary.tldr: GenCeption leverages a pre-trained video generative diffusion backbone for general-purpose vision, achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks with high data efficiency and emergent generalization capabilities.
key_points: GenCeption utilizes a pre-trained video generative diffusion backbone to create a feed-forward perception model for text-steered vision tasks.

It achieves state-of-the-art performance on tasks including depth, surface normal, camera pose estimation, expression-referring segmentation, and 3D keypoint prediction, often matching or surpassing specialized models (e.g., DepthAnything3, SAM3).
The video generative pretraining paradigm outperforms alternative pretraining methods like V-JEPA and Video MAE in comparable settings.
GenCeption demonstrates high data efficiency, achieving comparable performance to leading models (D4RT, VGGT-Omega) with 7 to 500 times less training data.
A model trained on synthetic human videos generalizes to real-world footage and out-of-distribution object categories (e.g., animals, robots).
summary.why_it_matters: This approach suggests that large-scale text-to-video generation can serve as a foundational pre-training paradigm for developing generalist computer vision models for the physical world.

papers.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading

summary.tldr: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench introduces a benchmark of 46 long-horizon terminal tasks with dense reward-based grading to evaluate AI agents on complex, multi-step workflows.
key_points: The benchmark comprises 46 long-horizon tasks across nine categories, including experiment reproduction, software engineering, and scientific computing.
Tasks are decomposed into fine-grained graded subtasks, enabling dense intermediate rewards and partial credit evaluation.
Tasks typically require hundreds of episodes and minutes to hours of execution, stressing long-horizon planning and long-context management.
Evaluation of 15 frontier models showed agents consumed an average of 9.9M tokens, 231 episodes, and 85.3 minutes per task run.
The strongest model achieved 15.2% pass@1 at a 0.95 partial-reward threshold and 10.9% at a 1.0 perfect-reward threshold, with a mean pass rate of 4.3% and 1.7% respectively across all models.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a more comprehensive evaluation of AI agent capabilities on complex, real-world terminal tasks by assessing intermediate progress and partial solutions.

papers.title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that visual pretraining on document images consistently outperforms text-only pretraining for language intelligence, challenging the assumption that language models must be trained solely on text.
key_points: Visual pretraining directly leverages visual documents without text extraction.
Systematic study of unsupervised visual pretraining paradigms was conducted.
Visual pretraining consistently outperforms text-only pretraining across multiple backbones and benchmarks using the same underlying corpora.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers an efficient pathway to scalable language intelligence by incorporating rich visual information often discarded in text-only pretraining.

papers.title: Trust Region Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Trust Region Policy Distillation (TOP-D) stabilizes On-Policy Distillation (OPD) by dynamically constructing a proximal teacher, controlling gradient variance, and improving training stability, sample efficiency, and performance without additional computational overhead.
key_points: TOP-D transforms unstable On-Policy Distillation (OPD) into a stable training paradigm.
It dynamically constructs a proximal teacher to control gradient variance.
A formal global convergence analysis and monotonic improvement bound are provided.
TOP-D enhances training stability, sample efficiency, and final performance on mathematical reasoning tasks.
It introduces zero additional computational overhead compared to OPD.
summary.why_it_matters: TOP-D offers a more reliable and efficient method for policy distillation, improving performance on complex tasks without increasing computational cost.

papers.title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian

summary.tldr: KronQ introduces a post-training quantization framework for LLMs that incorporates gradient covariance into the quantization objective, improving performance over existing second-order methods.
key_points: KronQ's quantization loss depends on both activation and gradient covariances, derived from a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation.
It implements bidirectional incoherence processing, extending input-side random rotation to the output dimension using gradient covariance to reduce weight magnitude variance.
KronQ develops a new sensitivity metric for inter-layer mixed-precision allocation, based on gradient and activation Hessian traces.
For 2-bit weight-only quantization on LLaMA-3-70B, KronQ achieved 7.93 perplexity on WikiText-2, while GPTQ and GPTAQ produced degenerate quantizations (>2000 perplexity).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more effective extreme quantization (e.g., 2-bit) for large language models, which is crucial for deploying them on resource-constrained hardware.

papers.title: From RGB Generation to Dense Field Readout: Pixel-Space Dense Prediction with Text-to-Image Models

summary.tldr: ReChannel adapts frozen DiT models for dense prediction by mapping tokens to task-native pixel-space patches via a minimal linear head, achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.
key_points: ReChannel reuses RGB-trained DiT models by dropping the target-side decoder and adapting the frozen DiT with task LoRA.
Instead of generating RGB content, ReChannel maps each DiT token to a p x p x K_t pixel-space patch using a shared token-local linear head (approx. 33K parameters).
Evaluated on FLUX-Klein, ReChannel achieves new state-of-the-art in trimap-free matting, KITTI depth, and referring segmentation.
ReChannel is 2.48x faster and more accurate than edit-plus-latent-decode counterparts in a matched 4B setting.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows dense perception tasks to leverage generative pretraining efficiently without inheriting the generative output interface, leading to improved performance and speed.

papers.title: Self-Guided Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs

summary.tldr: Self-Guided Test-Time Training (S-TTT) improves long-context LLM accuracy by adaptively selecting relevant evidence spans for instance-specific parameter adaptation, avoiding the cost and noise of full-context or random-span TTT.
key_points: Traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) on long contexts is computationally expensive, and random span sampling for TTT can degrade performance due to irrelevant information.
A preliminary study on LongBench-v2 showed TTT on random spans hurt performance, while TTT on oracle spans substantially improved it, highlighting sensitivity to training-span quality.
Self-Guided TTT (S-TTT) addresses this by having the model identify relevant evidence spans before adaptation, applying the standard language-modeling objective only to these selected spans.
S-TTT achieved up to a 15% relative accuracy improvement on LongBench-v2 and LongBench-Pro for Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more efficient and effective way to leverage long contexts in LLMs, improving their reasoning capabilities without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Towards Mechanistically Understanding Why Memorized Knowledge Fails to Generalize in Large Language Model Finetuning

summary.tldr: LLMs memorize new facts but fail to generalize them, a "Knowing--Using Gap" attributed to knowledge-circuit misalignment, where memorized representations are not routed to effective computational layers.
key_points: The "Knowing--Using Gap" describes LLMs memorizing new facts but failing to use them for downstream reasoning, characterized by an accuracy gap and temporal lag.
A novel self-patching intervention technique monitors spatial permeation dynamics of knowledge internally, identifying activation locations where representation relocation improves generalization.
The knowledge-circuit misalignment hypothesis suggests memorized representations exist internally but are not routed to computation-effective layers.
A heuristic strategy recovers 58-75% of the oracle headroom in generalization failure, demonstrating the diagnostic finding's practicality.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and mitigating the Knowing--Using Gap can improve LLM fine-tuning effectiveness for new knowledge injection.

papers.title: A Sovereign, Open-Source Foundation Model for German and English

summary.tldr: Soofi S 30B-A3B, a hybrid Mamba Transformer MoE model, achieves competitive performance on German and English benchmarks with 3B active parameters, outperforming larger European sovereign models.
key_points: Soofi S 30B-A3B is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) hybrid Mamba Transformer model with 30B total parameters, activating 3B parameters per token.
The model's hybrid design maintains a near-constant inference cache, providing a throughput advantage for long-context, high-concurrency deployment.
Pretrained on approximately 27 trillion tokens with up-weighted German data, Soofi S matches 14-27B dense models on aggregate English and German benchmarks.
Soofi S achieves the best code aggregates in both German and English among 17 open base models and outperforms all European sovereign baselines in comparison.

The model was developed on the German Industrial AI Cloud and will be released with weights, checkpoints, data accounting, hyperparameters, and training/evaluation code under permissive open-access terms.
summary.why_it_matters: This model offers a high-performance, open-source foundation for German and English language processing, suitable for efficient deployment in long-context, high-concurrency scenarios.

papers.title: MedPMC: A Systematic Framework for Scaling High-Fidelity Medical Multimodal Data for Foundation Models

summary.tldr: MedPMC is an automated framework that curates 11 million high-fidelity medical image-text pairs from 6.1 million PMC articles, improving multimodal foundation models.
key_points: MedPMC processed 6.1 million PMC articles to curate 11 million medical image-text pairs.
Component evaluations showed high F1 scores for initial screening (93.2), multi-panel figure detection (96.5), and medical figure classification (96.5).
Manual review found 95.3% of MedPMC images medically relevant, compared to 19.7% in a prior PMC-derived dataset.
A MedPMC-trained CLIP-style model improved average zero-shot AUC by 7.1 percentage points across 26 benchmarks and improved medical visual question-answering by up to 16.9 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a scalable source of high-quality medical multimodal data, addressing a key constraint in developing advanced medical AI models.

papers.title: Flow-ERD: Agent-type Aware Flow Matching with Entropy-Regularized Distillation for Diverse Traffic Simulation

summary.tldr: Flow-ERD introduces a multi-agent traffic simulator combining Agent-Type Aware Flow Matching (AFM) for type-specific kinematics and Entropy-Regularized Distillation (ERD) to jointly optimize realism and diversity in autonomous driving simulations.
key_points: Flow-ERD uses Agent-Type Aware Flow Matching (AFM) to couple flow matching's multi-modal expressiveness with type-specific kinematic execution, preserving fine-grained diversity.

Entropy-Regularized Distillation (ERD) fine-tunes the closed-loop rollout distribution using an entropy-regularized reverse-KL objective to mitigate covariate shift and prevent collapse onto high-density modes.
Flow-ERD is evaluated using a log-free diversity metric in addition to standard realism scores.
Flow-ERD ranks first on the WOSAC test benchmark and dominates the realism-diversity Pareto front among reproducible baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Improving both realism and diversity in traffic simulation is crucial for robust autonomous driving development and testing.

papers.title: VaseMuseum: Digital Intelligent Museum for Ancient Greek Pottery

summary.tldr: VaseMuseum is a multimodal agent framework for digital museums of ancient Greek pottery, using VaseAgent for 2D/3D artifact analysis, external knowledge retrieval, and inference-time reliability control to improve VLM accuracy.
key_points: VaseMuseum addresses VLM limitations in cultural heritage by integrating multimodal perception, 3D-aware reasoning, and external knowledge retrieval.
VaseAgent employs source-level control to select diverse, verifiable evidence from authoritative web and museum sources before generation.
Response-level control checks generated claims against an evidence pool, promoting neutral, evidence-bounded answers and calibrated uncertainty.
A training-free GRPO-style selection mechanism favors responses with valid references and calibrated confidence without VLM backbone updates.
summary.why_it_matters: VaseMuseum enhances the reliability and accuracy of interactive digital museums for cultural heritage by reducing hallucinations and improving citation validity in VLM responses.

papers.title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales

summary.tldr: This work adapts and enhances preconditioned gradient methods like SOAP and Muon for large-scale LLM pretraining, demonstrating improved stability and performance over AdamW at high batch sizes.
key_points: Identified and addressed SOAP instabilities at large batch sizes via per-step QR orthogonalization and improved preconditioning strategies.
Conducted a unified empirical study of SOAP, Muon, and AdamW using update-RMS matching on multi-billion-parameter models and trillions of tokens.
Demonstrated SOAP and Muon outperform AdamW, maintaining stability and quality at batch sizes up to 100M tokens for next-token prediction, where AdamW degrades.
Introduced a layer-wise distributed optimizer compatible with Megatron-LM, balancing memory and hiding communication without approximating optimizer computations.
Implemented system-level improvements to accelerate the layer-wise distributed optimizer and released a codebase for emerging optimization algorithms.
summary.why_it_matters: These advancements enable more efficient and stable pretraining of large language models using higher-order optimizers, potentially accelerating LLM development.

papers.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities

summary.tldr: This paper provides the first comprehensive overview of metacognition in LLMs, analyzing current knowledge, technical advancements, and future research directions in this emerging field.
key_points: The paper taxonomizes the landscape of metacognition for LLMs.
It summarizes recent technical advancements, including methods and benchmarks for measuring and evaluating LLM metacognitive abilities.
Techniques to elicit, improve, and apply metacognition in LLMs are discussed.
The review covers findings and implications of ongoing research in LLM metacognition.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and implementing metacognition in LLMs is crucial for developing more capable, transparent, and reliable AI systems.

papers.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a theoretical framework explaining Transformer inductive reasoning by confining learning dynamics to a low-dimensional invariant manifold, simplifying analysis of circuit formation and learning mechanisms.
key_points: The framework unifies synthetic inductive tasks like in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning.
Training dynamics of attention models are theoretically proven to be confined to a low-dimensional invariant manifold.
Learning dynamics on this manifold are captured by a few interpretable coordinates, not millions of parameters.
The framework characterizes how data statistics influence the competition between in-context and in-weights learning.
It demonstrates that the manifold's coordinate frame can automatically detect learned circuits in trained models.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework offers a more tractable approach to understanding and predicting how Transformers learn inductive reasoning circuits, moving towards a predictive theory of Transformer learning.

papers.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias

summary.tldr: This study provides a representation-level account of LLM-as-judge scoring bias, demonstrating that biases manifest as specific activation geometry in hidden states, enabling causal control and operational prediction of judge failures.
key_points: Baseline judging inputs occupy a tight activation manifold, while biased inputs are displaced along a low-dimensional, type-specific subspace that sharpens with depth and is consistently recovered by three estimator families.
Steering hidden states along this bias subspace causally drives scoring, with forward shifts reproducing biased scoring on clean inputs and reverse shifts restoring baseline scoring on biased inputs.
Matched-norm random directions produce scoring shifts an order of magnitude smaller than steering along the bias subspace.
A simple linear projection onto bias-direction features anticipates judge failures on three unseen benchmarks, outperforming text-based alternatives.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding LLM-as-judge bias as activation geometry allows for more effective diagnosis, mitigation, and prediction of scoring failures beyond input-output level analysis.

papers.title: Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming

summary.tldr: AHA is an automated red-teaming framework that uses an agentic research environment to discover reusable vulnerability knowledge in production LLM agents, outperforming frozen discovery baselines by 14.2 percentage points.
key_points: AHA employs a falsifiable discovery loop: proposes a vulnerability hypothesis, constructs a falsifier, instantiates an attack, executes it in a sandboxed harness, reflects on the trajectory, and promotes confirmed findings.

Confirmed findings are stored in a Vulnerability Concept Graph (VCG), linking attacker-facing surfaces to unsafe trajectories via claims, enabling conditions, falsifiers, transfer predictions, and evidence.
The VCG provides an auditable artifact for production safety teams to inspect vulnerabilities, validate patches, and accumulate reusable safety knowledge.
Across Claude Code and Codex on three scenarios (direct and indirect attacks), the discovered concepts revealed a reusable vulnerability core.
A frozen VCG outperforms the strongest frozen discovery baseline by 14.2 percentage points under the same single-shot protocol and transfers across scenarios and attack channels.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a systematic, automated approach for identifying and documenting vulnerabilities in production LLM agents, enhancing their safety and reliability.

papers.title: Sparse Inter-Layer Dependencies of Transformer FFN Neurons

summary.tldr: A training-free attribution method reveals sparse inter-layer dependencies within Transformer FFN neurons, showing that small subsets of upstream activations and attention outputs suffice to explain target neuron activations.
key_points: FFN neuron activation can be explained by a sparse set of preceding neuron activations and attention outputs, despite dense parameterization.
A training-free attribution method estimates the relative influence of upstream neurons and attention outputs on a target neuron's activation.
Small subsets of preceding activations and attention outputs preserve neuron activations with high fidelity when other inputs are masked with average values.
Applying neuron-specific masks across all layers simultaneously, at moderate sparsity, largely preserves model perplexity.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a scalable tool for circuit-level interpretability and identifies sparse pathways, potentially leading to more efficient Transformer inference.

papers.title: Extending LLM Context via Associative Recurrent Memory

summary.tldr: The Associative Recurrent Memory Transformer (ARMT) extends LLM context length with constant memory scaling and 30% fewer FLOPs, using domain-specific datasets and a comprehensive training recipe.
key_points: Two domain-specific long-context datasets were constructed for evaluating realistic workloads in narrow-domain fine-tuning.
A training recipe for ARMT includes continued pre-training, synthetic long-context data generation, curriculum learning, and selective associative memory integration into model layers.
ARMT-augmented models process inputs beyond original context limits without performance degradation and generalize to out-of-distribution context lengths.
ARMT-augmented models require 30% less FLOPs while maintaining baseline performance within the original context window.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables LLMs to handle significantly longer contexts efficiently, addressing a critical limitation for real-world applications.

papers.title: Forgetful Attention: A Trainable Support-Vector Memory with Certified Selection and Exact Unlearning

summary.tldr: SV-Attention introduces a max-margin memory based on a one-class SVM, enabling certified output-preserving token eviction and exact unlearning through a reversible incremental solver.
key_points: SV-Attention uses a one-class SVM with fixed box parameter C, where weights are support coefficients, allowing reserve tokens to have zero weight for certified eviction.
A reversible incremental solver deletes tokens, recovering the state as if retrained without them, with decision functions matching to 10^-9 median deviation in fp64 experiments.
The exact deletion path reuses a maintained KKT inverse in a custom backward pass, while training uses a separate batched approximation.
Certified selection achieves 0.86 vs. 0.32 rare-item recall and 0.80 vs. 0.05 deterioration hours on MIMIC-IV streams at matched budgets.
On enwik8, the hybrid model achieves 2.178 BPC, an 8.6% improvement over a matched-state sliding-window Transformer (2.383 BPC).
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides certified control over memory content and influence, enabling reliable unlearning and selective retention in attention mechanisms.

papers.title: Securing LLMs in the Wild: Privacy and Security Challenges at the Edge

summary.tldr: This paper introduces the Security-Efficiency Paradox for edge LLMs, detailing how aggressive optimizations for limited compute and memory can introduce vulnerabilities and reshape the threat landscape.
key_points: The Security-Efficiency Paradox describes how LLM efficiency optimizations (quantization, pruning, partitioning, adaptation) can degrade robustness, expose attack surfaces, or increase privacy risks.
A deployment-centric taxonomy categorizes risks based on architectural constraints: Memory Wall, Quadratic Wall, and Compute Wall, linking them to specific attack surfaces.

The Secure Operational Efficiency Score (SOES) is proposed as a holistic metric balancing task accuracy, jailbreak resistance, and privacy against energy, memory, and latency for edge LLM configuration.

The paper provides a unified constraint model quantifying when unsafe optimizations become unavoidable and offers a practical decision procedure with targeted mitigations for optimization-induced vulnerabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables practitioners to jointly evaluate and secure edge LLMs by balancing security, privacy, and efficiency under real-world hardware limitations.

papers.title: From Expressivity to Sample Complexity: Narrow Teachers for Transformers via C-RASP

summary.tldr: This work proposes preliminary sample complexity bounds for learning C-RASP constructions with Transformers, moving towards understanding learnability in attention-based models.
key_points: The paper addresses the learnability of solutions in Transformer models, a gap in existing theoretical work.
It proposes preliminary sample complexity bounds.
The bounds are specifically for learning C-RASP constructions with Transformers.
The approach is inspired by recent loss landscape analysis work.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the learnability of Transformers can help characterize the capacities and limitations of large language models.

papers.title: When Local Monitors Miss Compositional Harm: Diagnosing Distributed Backdoors in Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: This paper demonstrates that local runtime monitors in multi-agent LLM systems fail to detect distributed backdoors where harmful payloads are split across agents, appearing benign until reassembled.
key_points: Distributed backdoors exploit an "observability boundary" where individual fragments appear benign to local monitors, making detection impossible within that view.
A monitor trained solely on benign traffic can recover the attack's code structure across held-out encodings, achieving a 0.874 mean AUROC.
Full-trace monitors and decoders fail unless they access the representation where the distributed payload is exposed.
Local safety checks are insufficient for global safety when harm is compositional across multiple agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Current local monitoring strategies for multi-agent LLM systems are fundamentally vulnerable to compositional attacks, necessitating new detection methods that operate on assembled or exposed representations of payloads.

papers.title: SCOPE-RL: Optimizing Reasoning Paths Before and After Success

summary.tldr: SCOPE-RL densifies sparse verifiable rewards in RLVR for LLMs by introducing two stages: Adaptive Scaffolded RL for pre-success reasoning and Quality-Aware Process RL for post-success refinement.
key_points: SCOPE-RL uses Adaptive Scaffolded RL to add prefix-decomposed verifiable rewards on answer-hidden sub-question chains before success.
Quality-Aware Process RL applies correctness-gated process-shape rewards to refine correct trajectories after success.
An expert-validated Step-Quality Evaluation Protocol assesses useful-step density, error localization, and token efficiency.
On Qwen3-8B-Instruct, SCOPE-RL improved average accuracy by up to 11.2 percentage points and reduced reasoning tokens by up to 27.1% over outcome-only GRPO.
The gains were observed across different models (Qwen3-0.6B-Instruct) and policy updates (GSPO), indicating reward-signal densification's complementarity.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves LLM reasoning accuracy and efficiency by providing more granular feedback during the problem-solving process.

papers.title: HyperSafe: Inference-Time Safety Recovery for Fine-Tuned Language Models

summary.tldr: HyperSafe introduces a post hoc, model-specific, and non-invasive framework to restore safety in fine-tuned language models by generating a Safe Side Network (SSN) for prompt-level safety classification.
key_points: HyperSafe generates a model-specific Safe Side Network (SSN) for each fine-tuned checkpoint using layer-wise activation fingerprints and calibration prompts.
The SSN operates alongside the frozen fine-tuned model, routing harmful prompts to refusal and safe prompts to the original model, without gradient updates or weight modification.
Evaluations on Qwen2-7B and LLaMA-3-8B models show HyperSafe reduces harmful response rates from 19-31% to below 1% on held-out checkpoints.
HyperSafe maintains downstream task accuracy within 1% of the fine-tuned baseline on average.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a cost-effective and non-invasive way to restore safety in fine-tuned LLMs without compromising task performance or requiring retraining.

infra.title: Modernizing the Meta Ads Service With an Open-Source Kernel Scheduler

summary.tldr: Meta modernized its Ads service using sched_ext, an open-source, BPF-based kernel scheduler, to create a workload-specific scheduling policy, resulting in a 28% reduction in ads retrieval tail latency and a 1.1% increase in ads ranked.
key_points: The sched_ext framework, which officially entered kernel v6.12, allows developers to implement custom scheduling policies as BPF programs.
The custom policy soft-partitions CPUs into two pools: one for latency-critical request path threads and another for less latency-sensitive work, with dynamic pool sizing based on load heuristics.
This approach improves L3 cache locality and reduces DRAM access by keeping related work on the same CPUs.
The policy is packaged as a user-space binary, enabling rapid experimentation and performance optimization without kernel rebuilds.
Deployment addressed a latency regression observed with the EEVDF scheduler in Linux kernel v6.6 during a fleet upgrade to kernel v6.9.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing kernel scheduling for specific workloads like ad serving directly translates to improved performance metrics, power savings, and increased business value at Meta's scale.
